agent_session_id.description: The sidechain session the agent runs in.

Attachment.description:
Something the user attached to their message — a pasted screenshot, a
dragged-in file, an editor selection.

The variants below are the three shapes hosts actually have, so that a host
can hand over whichever it already holds instead of being forced to pre-read
(or pre-decode) on the runtime's behalf.

oneOf.description:
A path the runtime should read. Images (by extension) become
[`ModelContentBlock::Image`], `.pdf` into [`ModelContentBlock::Document`];
anything else is inlined as text.
Use this when the host only has a path — e.g. a drag-and-drop.

Text the host has already read. `path` is kept for the label shown to
the model, and may be a synthetic name for non-file text such as an
editor selection.

An image the host already decoded — the clipboard-paste case, where
there is no file on disk at all. `data` is base64 without a data-URI
prefix.

A PDF the host already encoded. `data` is base64 without a data-URI
prefix; `name` is the label the model and the provider see.

blob.description: `s.<id>` a system block, `m.<id>` a message, `t.<id>` the tool table.

bytes.description: Length of the JSON `session.callBlob` answers with.

anyOf.description: Written by whoever configured this deployment.

the host named it.

An entry of a `settings.prompt.append` list a settings file gave,

BlockRole.description:

whenever such a block differs, as the skills inventory does between
projects.

PermissionDecision.description:
Wire shape: `{"type":"permit"}` / `{"type":"deny","reason":"..."}` /
`{"type":"permit_always","scope":"session"}` /
`{"type":"permit_always","scope":"local"}` — what
`session.respondToPrompt` (daemon RPC) parses out of its `decision`
param and what `InputMessage::PermissionResponse` carries.

oneOf.description:
Like `Permit`, but also persists an Allow rule beyond this single
tool call — see `base::interface::permission::PermissionGrants`.
`scope: Session` keeps it in-memory only (rest of this session);
`scope: Local` additionally writes it to the project directory's
`settings.local.json`, so future sessions in this project inherit it too.
Prompt user for each tool call that isn't explicitly allowed.

Allow file writes inside the project (the working directory and
`files.extra_dirs`) and read-only calls without asking;
ask about the rest, as `default` does. Writes into the project's
`.git`, its project directory (`.agix` unless renamed; then `.agix`
too), `.claude` and `.agents/skills` still ask.

Ask nothing and skip the rules of the user's tiers. Credentials
(`.ssh`, `.aws`, `.gnupg`, the state directory's settings and tokens)
are still refused, the deployment's managed `deny` / `ask` rules still
apply, input that is not valid is still refused, and `Bash` still runs
in the OS sandbox.
Plan mode — only allow read-only tools.
Don't ask — deny any tool not explicitly allowed (no prompt).

SessionOptions.description:
Optional per-session configuration passed via `session.create` or
`session.run_turn` params.

Taken when the session is created and kept with it: every rebuild of the
session's engine — a settings change, an idle eviction, a daemon restart —
applies the same options again. Options sent with a later call to an
existing session are ignored, except by `session.create` under the
session's id, which refuses ones other than it was created with.

attended.description:
Whether someone answers this session's questions and permission
prompts; `None` is its scene's `interactive`. Its sub-agents and team
members are attended as it is.

auto_name.description:
`false`: the session is not named after its first turn, its name is
left to `session.rename`. `None` or `true`: as its scene says.

clock.description:
Where this session's kept time starts (the date in its prompt, its log's timestamps).
Omitted: the machine's clock — except in replay, where it starts when the recording did.

host_tools.description:
Tools this session's host runs itself, offered to the model as the
session's own; a call to one is a `host_tool_call` frame, answered
with `session.respondToolCall`.

model.description:
The conversation's model: a tier — `strong`, `balanced`, `fast` — or a
model id. `None` takes `model.tasks.main`'s tier.

output_schema.description:
JSON Schema the session's structured output must satisfy — see
`runtime::agent::Builder::output_schema`.

prompt_types.description:
The kinds of `prompt` frame this session's host answers: `permission`
always, `question` and `mcp_elicitation` when listed. Names this daemon does not know are
ignored rather than voiding the options.

provider.description:
A provider, by its id in `providers`, put first in this session's
`model.order` — for its conversation, sub-agents, compaction and every
other call; the rest of the order follows as the settings have it.
`None` keeps the settings' order.

settings.description:
Settings for this session, its sub-agents and its team members, in
the shape of a settings file, over the settings of its project and
scene: its reasoning effort and thinking (`model.effort`,
`model.thinking`) and system prompt (`prompt.append`,
`prompt.override`) among them. Judged as an untrusted project's
settings are, against the settings as they are each time the engine
is built — see `settings::overlay` and [`Self::settings_problems`].

Skill directories of the host's for this session, merged over the
tiers by name: a built-in, a package's or an untrusted project's skill
yields to one of these; the user's tiers and a trusted project's do
not. Of two listed directories the first wins a name. Read-only to
every session.

`not_set`, `applied`, `clamped`, `managed_overrode`,
`not_session_scope`, `ignored`, or `overridden` when the session
decided otherwise since (`session.setPermissionMode`).
